title: Quantile regression to examine the association of air pollution with subclinical atherosclerosis in an adolescent population.
ehr_evidence: Participants were part of the Prevention and Incidence of Asthma and Mite Allergy (PIAMA) population-based birth cohort established in the Netherlands in 1996; data came from parent/child questionnaires and medical examinations, with air pollution exposure estimated from ESCAPE land-use regression models.
summary: In a cross-sectional analysis of 363 16-year-olds from the PIAMA Dutch birth cohort, quantile regression was used to examine associations of childhood air pollution exposure (NO2, PM2.5, PM2.5 absorbance, PMcoarse, ultrafine particles) with carotid intima-media thickness (CIMT), a marker of subclinical atherosclerosis.
key_findings: PM2.5 absorbance (black carbon) exposure at birth was the only statistically significant association (FDR < 0.05), associated with a 6.23 μm (95% CI: 0.15, 12.30) higher CIMT per IQR increment at the 10th quantile of CIMT, but not at the 50th (estimate 1.69 μm, 95% CI: −5.59, 8.97) or 90th quantile (estimate −4.54 μm, 95% CI: −12.11, 3.03).

NO2 exposure at birth showed a similar effect size but much wider confidence interval (10th quantile estimate 7.11 μm, 95% CI: −17.1, 31.32) and was not statistically significant after FDR correction.

PM2.5 exposure at birth was weakly associated (p < 0.10) with higher CIMT at the 10th quantile (4.85 μm, 95% CI: −0.41, 10.10) and 20th quantile (3.73 μm, 95% CI: −0.74, 8.20) but not significant after FDR correction.
PMcoarse and ultrafine particles showed no statistically significant associations nor consistent patterns across any CIMT quantiles.
captured_features: Carotid intima-media thickness (CIMT) measured by ultrasound at age 16
Annual air pollution concentrations (NO2, PM2.5, PM2.5 absorbance, PMcoarse, ultrafine particles) assigned at residential birth addresses from ESCAPE land-use regression and national ultrafine models
Age, sex, BMI, total cholesterol, HDL cholesterol, systolic and diastolic blood pressure
Parental education, indoor tobacco smoke exposure, maternal smoking during pregnancy, maternal BMI, breastfeeding status, Dutch nationality
pathologies_diseases: Subclinical atherosclerosis (measured by carotid intima-media thickness)
study_design: Cross-sectional analysis within a population-based birth cohort
population: 363 adolescents aged 16 years from the PIAMA population-based birth cohort in the Netherlands
exposure_domain: Air pollution (NO2, PM2.5, PM2.5 absorbance/black carbon, PMcoarse, ultrafine particles)
limitations: Cross-sectional design with only one CIMT measurement, so findings cannot support causal inference.
Air pollution exposure was estimated only at residential addresses and did not account for school or other non-home exposure.
Low performance of the PMcoarse exposure model (leave-one-out cross-validation R2 = 38%).
Exposure models accounted for spatial but not temporal trends in air pollution.
